lead.title: Australian politics live: Chalmers says unemployment rise a ‘very bad development’; Liberals ‘tossing up whether to leave or remain’, PM says
lead.summary: Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Pauline Hanson has released a statement this morning welcoming South Australian senator Leah Blyth to her party . Blyth is the second high-profile federal defection from the Coalition to One Nation – after Barnaby Joyce . Senator Blyth will be One Nation’s first South Australian Senator and will build on One Nation’s expanding support within the state. My team and I are delighted to welcome Senator Blyth to sit in the Senate with One Nation. We are facing at the next election clearly a coalition of the Liberals, Nationals and One Nation, with all the baggage that each of these parties brings to the table. They’re all anti-worker, they’re all extreme … this demonstrates, I think, more disunity in the Liberal party under Angus Taylor . Continue reading...

top.title: Flinders Island bushfire: Out-of-control fire with flames 10-metres high destroys at least six homes in Tasmania
top.summary: Fire making a ‘significant run’ towards the south-west of Flinders Island on Thursday, Tasmania Fire Service says Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Residents in the north of Flinders Island in Tasmania have been told to take shelter, as an out-of-control bushfire destroys homes and sends smoke hundreds of kilometres south. By Thursday midday, the uncontrolled fire involving 10-metre high flames had burned through 14,500 hectares – about 10% of the island – with at least six properties damaged or destroyed and authorities warning more were at risk. top.title: Coalition would privatise Melbourne’s sewage treatment while selling state land and renewables to fund Victorian election promises and cut debt
top.summary: Liberal and Nationals’ pre-election policy costings also reveal that ‘air rights’ between Richmond train station and the MCG would be sold Follow our Australia politics live blog for latest updates Victorian election 2026 guide: what you need to know Confused about who to vote for? Check the parties’ key promises and policies Get our daily political email , free app or daily news podcast A Victorian Coalition government would privatise two sewage plants and sell off state-owned land, renewable energy assets and the “air rights” between Richmond train station and the Melbourne Cricket Ground if elected. The opposition leader, Jess Wilson, released the Liberal and Nationals’ pre-election policy costings on Thursday, just two days before the state election and after more than 1.5m Victorians have already cast their vote. Labor, which has been releasing its costings throughout the campaign, provided its overall budget projections. Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here . Continue reading...
